verified_facts.text: The hotel is in Lisbon's historic center, between Chiado and Bairro Alto.
verified_facts.excerpt: Bairro Alto Hotel is located in the historic center of Lisbon in a prestigious and emblematic area, made even more special by the several Lisbon sights it offers: it is located between the elegant and cosmopolitan Chiado and the bohemian Bairro Alto.

verified_facts.text: Praca Luis de Camoes is visible from the hotel's entrance.
verified_facts.excerpt: From the entrance of the hotel we see Praça Luís de Camões, which imposes itself as a separation between this neighborhood and Chiado.

verified_facts.text: The hotel is housed in an 18th-century building with a primrose yellow exterior on Praca Luis de Camoes.
verified_facts.excerpt: The distinctive, primrose yellow exterior of the 18th-century building that houses the Bairro Alto Hotel has an impressive perch on the edge of Chiado’s landmark square, the Praça Luís de Camões
First opened in 2005, before Lisbon became one of Europe’s hot spots

verified_facts.text: The hotel reopened in 2019 after a three-year renovation.
verified_facts.excerpt: It reopened in 2019 following a three-year renovation.

verified_facts.text: The hotel spans four Pombal-era buildings, so no two rooms are the same.
verified_facts.excerpt: The hotel is larger and now spans four Pombal-era buildings, so no two rooms are the same.

verified_facts.text: The interiors include specially commissioned pieces by Portuguese artists such as Vasco Araujo and Rui Chafes.
verified_facts.excerpt: specially commissioned pieces from Portuguese artists like Vasco Araújo and Rui Chafes

verified_facts.text: Rooms have soundproofed windows that block out the noise of passing trams.
verified_facts.excerpt: Special mention goes to the soundproofed windows, which block out the rumble of the city’s yellow trams as they pass.

verified_facts.text: The fifth-floor restaurant serves Portuguese cuisine created by Chef Bruno Rocha.
verified_facts.excerpt: Go up to the 5th floor and be amazed by the best of Portuguese cuisine, created by Chef Bruno Rocha

verified_facts.text: The ground-floor Patisserie makes Portuguese sweet and savoury pastries in the hotel throughout the day.
verified_facts.excerpt: oﬀers a daily selection of typically Portuguese sweet and savoury pastries freshly made in the hotel throughout the day.

verified_facts.text: The Mezzanine bar on the ground floor serves healthy meals throughout the day.
verified_facts.excerpt: Welcoming and cosy, on a mezzanine on the ground ﬂoor, this bar is the hotel’s meeting point par excellence. You can enjoy our menu of healthy meals throughout the day.

verified_facts.text: A sixth-floor bar is reserved for hotel residents, with views over the rooftops to the River Tagus.
verified_facts.excerpt: only hotel residents can use the sixth-floor bar, a secret spot where blue skies stretch out over the rooftops to the River Tagus

verified_facts.text: The hotel's terrace has a view over the city and the Tejo river.
verified_facts.excerpt: This is the place for those who want to enjoy an incomparable view over the city and the Tejo river.

verified_facts.text: The wellness center has a Susanne Kaufmann spa and a gym.
verified_facts.excerpt: Even with its on-trend Susanne Kaufmann spa, the wellness center, which also includes a gym, still feels like a bit of an afterthought.

verified_facts.text: The hotel is a member of The Leading Hotels of the World.
verified_facts.excerpt: A member of The Leading Hotels of the World, Bairro Alto Hotel is a pioneer

verified_facts.text: The hotel offers guests a guide to Lisbon with off-radar suggestions.
verified_facts.excerpt: There’s also a useful guide to Lisbon with some genuinely off-radar suggestions.

verified_facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler notes there are no especially child-friendly corners.
verified_facts.excerpt: Weekending couples and some families from both sides of the Atlantic, although there are no especially child-friendly corners.

verified_facts.text: It is a steep walk down the hill to the banks of the River Tagus.
verified_facts.excerpt: It’s a steep stroll down the hill to the banks of the River Tagus.

verified_facts.text: Tram 28 passes through Chiado near the hotel.
verified_facts.excerpt: Under the watchful eye of Fernando Pessoa, a tram goes by: the "28", as it is known, in operation for more than 100 years.
